messages:
anna_dev: Quick summary -- ran a targeted perf sweep comparing FlashAttn v2 vs v3 + fused fallback on paged-attn workload (8xA100). Posting numbers and hypotheses; want thoughts on kernel pick heuristics + rollout flags before we ship.

michael_r: awesome, paste p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec and cost delta when you have it.

anna_dev: key results: v3 improves p50 by ~18% for short (<=512) and mid (512-4k) contexts, tokens/sec +14% overall. For >16k contexts v2 is ~6% faster p50. p99: v3 had intermittent spikes (up to +45% vs v2) tied to KV page remap work under eviction bursts. Estimated GPU-ms/token down ~10% avg -> ~11% token-cost reduction.

sanjay_m: what's the test mix and batching settings? also page size?

anna_dev: benchmark snippet:
```
model: redwood-llm-70b
hardware: 8xA100-40GB
mix: 50% <=512, 30% 512-4096, 20% 4096-32768
batching: dyn_window_ms=10, max_batch=48, prefer_contiguous=true
kv: paged_attn=true, page_size=32k, hot_ratio=0.75
kernels: flashattn-v2 | flashattn-v3 | fused-attn
metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, gpu-ms-per-token, page_eviction_rate
```

eva_perf: interesting. Evictions caused by what pattern?

anna_dev: v3's tiled KV layout uses denser metadata which accelerates in-core ops, but it also triggers remap/compaction when active set churn > ~5% of pages. Under high concurrency that remap runs on critical path and aligns with those p99 spikes. v2 keeps a simpler linear layout so remap cost is less frequent.

michael_r: sounds like a policy + sizing issue rather than an inherent kernel bug. Can we adjust eviction policy or reserve head-room to avoid remaps?

anna_dev: yes. I ran a retest with kv_eviction_profile=conservative and increased page-reserve from 8%->20%; spikes reduced ~80% while v3 median stayed the same. So solution: tune cache defaults for v3, or route sensitive flows to v2.

sanjay_m: batching heuristics? v3 needs packed homogeneous lengths to hit vectorized paths, right?

anna_dev: exactly. v3 benefits from tighter length groups. With dyn_window_ms=10 we mix lengths; adding a short staging bin (hold up to 5ms to regroup by binned length) improved tokens/sec by ~9% with minimal added tail for 95% of requests.

michael_r: tradeoff. We should gate this behind a flag and expose "latency_opt" vs "throughput_opt".

anna_dev: proposing feature flags:
- ff/attn_strategy: "auto" | "prefer_v3" | "prefer_v2" | "force_fused"
- ff/attn_bin_ms: integer (ms)
- ff/kv_eviction_profile: "aggressive" | "balanced" | "conservative"
- ff/attn_fallback_thresholds: json-string (e.g. "page_eviction_pct=3;p99_delta_ms=150")

eva_perf: add telemetry fields: kernel_label, page_evictions_per_min, kv_cache_fill_pct, batching_bins_hit. perf-bot should tag runs.

perf-bot: perf job scheduled: attn-integration-sweep-nightly -> results posted to https://internal.redwood/perf/attn-int?orgId=1

ops-bot: created canary group: flash-attn-integ-canary-5pct; alert on p99+20% lasting 5m.

deploy-bot: canary rollout created by @michael_r -> group flash-attn-integ-canary-5pct; monitoring hooks attached.

sanjay_m: rollout plan suggestion:
1) default ff/attn_strategy="auto" on staging; enable kernel telemetry & binning disabled.
2) run 72h A/B on staging: compare auto vs prefer_v3 with conservative kv profile.
3) if staging p99 stable, deploy 5% prod to canary group with kv_profile=conservative and attn_bin_ms=0.
4) monitor 24h; if stable, enable attn_bin_ms=5 for that canary (length-binning) -> monitor 24h.
5) ramp to 25% with attn_bin_ms=5 and then to 50% then full with fallback rule to prefer_v2 when page_eviction_pct > 2% over 1m.

eva_perf: add nightly long-context stress (sustained 32k seq for 2h) into CI; add alerting on regression vs baseline.

michael_r: I'll own PR review. Anna: please include CSVs and an explanation of the cache-tuning knobs you used. Sanjay: add an ops-runbook entry under eng-runtime/runbooks/ with exact ff names and fallback playbook.

anna_dev: will open PR with kernel selection logic + flags + a hidden opt-in for length-binning. attaching raw csvs in PR.

sanjay_m: I added a short checklist in runbooks: pre-canary checks, rollout thresholds, rollback steps, and where to find perf dashboards.

eva_perf: once we have telemetry hooked, let's make an automatic alert if kernel_label distribution flips unexpectedly.

anna_dev: TL;DR: v3 gives solid median & cost wins for typical mixes but needs KV-conservative defaults + optional length-binning to avoid p99 spikes. Feature flags + staged canary recommended. :white_check_mark:

michael_r: great thread. sync tomorrow 10am to approve PR.

ops-bot: reminder: flash-attn-integ-canary-5pct live; will auto-undo if p99 alert fires"
